title: Render
summary: The final shot: Eevee set up first (128 samples, Standard view), then the main spot becomes a big square area panel from the front-left of the camera (4500 K) with the warm back light raised; a brighter, glossier croissant, bigger sugar crystals, a blue tablecloth with small white squares turned slightly on Z, a softer depth of field (f/2.8), and the final render in Cycles with denoise.

objects.name: Foco
objects.description: now the big square key panel, front-left

objects.name: Mantel
objects.description: blue with small white squares, slightly rotated

expected_result: A finished square render: plate with sugared donuts in focus, croissant back left and white mug back right softly blurred, on a blue tablecloth with a white square pattern, soft light from the front-left and a warm rim from behind.

steps.note: first the Eevee setup the tutor recommends for most computers: render samples 128, shadows and ray tracing on, Color Management view Standard (what an sRGB image really looks like), output JPEG 90

the spot turned into an area light (Cycles gives it spread), a giant square panel in front-left of the camera aimed at the donuts, moved close; with Cycles its strength lowered (15 was too much once close), 4500 K so the scene is not so warm
the back (rim) light raised so it lights the scene from that side
the croissant came out dark: a little more light in its colour, less roughness for a little shine
the donuts barely showed their sugar: particles > render > scale up a little (too much, then back)
the same on the other donut
the tablecloth pattern changed: a much wider mortar in blue leaves small white squares; the weave bump softer (distortion and strength)
an imperfection: the tablecloth turned a little on Z so it is not perfectly lined up with the camera
the blur at f/1 was too much: F-stop 2.8
then Cycles: much better light (the tutor renders 500 samples; 256 with denoise is clean), denoise on, view Standard
